title: Number Complement Problem

notes: Only significant bits are complemented; leading zero bits are not part of the representation.
An all-ones mask with the same bit width as num flips exactly those significant bits.
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

sampleTestCases.explanation: The binary representation of 5 is 101 (no leading zero bits), and its complement is 010. So you need to output 2.
The binary representation of 1 is 1 (no leading zero bits), and its complement is 0. So you need to output 0.

content.problemStatement:
The **complement** of an integer is the integer you get when you flip all the `0`'s to `1`'s and all the `1`'s to `0`'s in its binary representation.

* As an example, The integer `5` is `"101"` in binary and its **complement** is `"010"` which is the integer `2`.

With an integer `num`, output *its complement*.

**Example 1:**

```
Input: num = 5
Output: 2
Explanation: The binary representation of 5 is 101 (no leading zero bits), and its complement is 010. So you need to output 2.
```

**Example 2:**

```
Input: num = 1
Output: 0
Explanation: The binary representation of 1 is 1 (no leading zero bits), and its complement is 0. So you need to output 0.
```

**Constraints:**

* `1 <= num < 2^31`

**Note:** This question is the same as 1009: <https://leetcode.com/problems/complement-of-base-10-integer/>

notes: Expected output is the JSON-serialised integer returned by findComplement.
A full-width NOT would also flip bits outside num’s significant representation.
solution.approach: Construct an all-ones mask across the significant bits of num and XOR it with num.

better.complexity: O(log num) time and O(1) extra space.
better.description: Iterate through the significant bits and build the complemented result bit by bit.

optimal.complexity: O(log num) time and O(1) extra space.
optimal.description: Build a same-width all-ones mask and XOR it with num.

bruteForce.complexity: O(log num) time and O(log num) extra space.
bruteForce.description: Convert num to binary, flip every significant bit, then convert back.

followUps: How can the mask be built using shifts and OR?
Why is bitwise NOT not directly correct here?
